The matrix is symmetric even though the graph is not: the one-way arc A to B gives -0.35 in both the A, B and B, A cells (highlighted), the chord -0.25, and B and D, with no arc, 0." width="100%"} The ordinary Laplacian of a directed graph is not symmetric, which breaks most spectral tools. Chung (2005) defines a symmetric directed Laplacian from a random walk on the graph: `L = I - (Φ^½ P Φ^-½ + Φ^-½ Pᵀ Φ^½) / 2`, where `P` is the walk's transition matrix and `Φ` its stationary distribution. Its eigenvalues are real, the smallest is `0`, and it supports a directed version of Cheeger's inequality and spectral partitioning. The walk follows NetworkX's `directed_laplacian_matrix()`: with `walk_type=None` it is an ordinary random walk if the graph is strongly connected and aperiodic, a lazy walk (staying put half the time) if it is strongly connected but periodic, and otherwise a PageRank walk that teleports with probability `1 - alpha`, which guarantees a unique stationary distribution. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [walk_type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"random"`, `"lazy"`, `"pagerank"`, or `None` (default) to choose automatically as described above. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Damping factor of the PageRank walk, strictly between `0` and `1`. Default is `0.95`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether transition probabilities follow edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the symmetric matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, `walk_type=` or `alpha=` is invalid, or a random or lazy walk is requested on a graph with a node without out-edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The result is symmetric even though the graph is not: ::: {#d5cf368c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) cycle.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("A", "C")]) matrix, nodes = cycle.directed_laplacian_matrix() [[round(v, 3) for v in row] for row in matrix] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [[1.0, -0.354, -0.75], [-0.354, 1.0, -0.354], [-0.75, -0.354, 1.0]] ``` ::: :::
